name: Sam Bush
notes: The progressive-bluegrass mandolin idiom: "the player who imported rock rhythm into the chop and thereby created the archetype's aggressive setting". The section's own scope note says why this entry looks the way it does: "in this archetype the producer role is largely occupied by instrumental specialists — the players whose parts are the train beat when there is no drum kit, and who also produce records. Each entry below is written as a parameter set for the part they contribute, because that is what the engine needs." His entry is the bluntest case of it: the Drums line reads "n/a — he *is* the drum part", so the drum block here is a chop specification. The entry gives it exactly: "the mandolin chop is a fully-damped four-string strike on the backbeat; his contribution is playing it with rock-drummer dynamics and displacement (accenting the and or dropping a chop for a bar as a fill). Model the chop as a velocity-and-placement layer ... and allow the chop to syncopate here where traditional bluegrass would not." That is the loudest accent tier in the bluegrass wing (104–124, rock-drummer dynamics against the wing's 76–102), a `percs` layer of rim and woodblock set to `placement` offbeat at [2,4] per bar — the direct encoding of "accenting the and" and the only offbeat percussion placement in this section — and `fills` back at 8/16 so a chop can drop for a bar. `snare.offGridMs` −4 is the driven placement the section names as the feel control; the loosest humanize of the bluegrass wing carries the rock dynamics. Harmony follows the stated widening: "his progressive designation means a wider chord vocabulary than the I–IV–V norm — add9, sus, 6th and dominant-7th voicings in the mandolin's four-string double-stops, plus modal vamps for improvisation", so `extensions` runs 0.50/0.36/0.14, `susSubstitutionProb` is 0.38 and a modal i–♭VII vamp sits in the families with a `vamp` share in the harmonic rhythm. The melody is his other documented native language: he won the National Fiddle Championship at 15, "so fiddle-tune melodic construction (continuous 8ths, scalar runs, drone double-stops) is native to his lead lines" — a 7–12 density with an 0.84 step share. ⚠ The entry says outright that "the chop parameterisation is my formalisation of a sourced technique [LOW-CONF]", and that flag applies to every drum number above. ⚠ Also INFERRED: `bpm.mode` 160 inside the stated 110–210, the velocity tiers, and every countermelody and bassline number.
